name: Alert
layerWhy: It says one fact about the place it sits in; acting on the fact is up to the page.
promise: Something about this place is true, and stays true until it changes.
expectation: A message above what it is about that won't go away until the situation does.
evidence: Its tone is a mark and words as well as colour; it has no close button; a banner variant speaks for the whole product.
behaviour: With [live], appearing after load, it is announced (danger urgently).
context: Above the page, section or form it is about. Not for the result of an action just taken.
relationships: Its place is "alert" (or "banner") in the behaviour model.
Its actions sit inside it, under the words.
accessibility: role="status" or role="alert" only when it appears after load.
The mark is drawn by CSS, the words carry the meaning.
failures: Never dismissible: a fact is changed, not hidden.
do: Title the fact; say what to do in the body.
dont: Several alerts stacked about one thing.

usage.markup: Renew it to keep your reports.
